passages.text: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John the brother of James, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Six days passed.
Jesus chose three disciples.
He chose Peter.
He chose James.
He chose John, the brother of James.
Jesus took these three men with Him.
Jesus led them up a high mountain.
They went by themselves.
No one else went with them.
passages.original: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν

passages.text: There He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before Peter, James, and John.
Jesus changed in appearance in front of them.
His face shone brightly like the sun.
His clothes became white like light.
passages.original: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς

passages.text: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood on the mountain with His disciples.
Peter, James, and John were with Him.
Suddenly, Moses appeared to them.
Elijah also appeared to them.
Moses and Elijah talked with Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, I will put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Lord, it is good for us to be here.”
Peter offered to build three shelters.
Peter said, “If You wish, I will make three shelters.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for You.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for Moses.”
Peter said, “One shelter will be for Elijah.”
passages.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ Κύριε καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι εἰ θέλεις ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν

passages.text: While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud enveloped them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was still speaking.
A bright cloud appeared.
The cloud covered them.
A voice came from the cloud.
The voice spoke clearly.
The voice said, “This is my beloved Son.
I am well pleased with Him.
Listen to Him.”
passages.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When the disciples heard this, they fell facedown in terror.
passages.sermon: The disciples heard the voice from the cloud.\r\nThey fell facedown on the ground.\r\nThey were very afraid.
passages.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα

passages.text: Then Jesus came over and touched them. “Get up,” He said. “Do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the disciples.
The disciples had fallen facedown in fear.
Jesus came to them.
He touched them.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Get up.”
He said, “Do not be afraid.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε

passages.text: And when they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
passages.sermon: The disciples looked up.\r\nThey saw no one else.\r\nThey saw only Jesus.
passages.original: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον

passages.text: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “Do not tell anyone about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
They were coming down the mountain.
Jesus spoke to them.
He gave them a command.
He said, “Do not tell anyone about this vision.
Wait until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
passages.original: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ

passages.text: The disciples asked Him, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “Why do the scribes say this?”
They said, “Elijah must come first.”
The scribes are teachers of the law.
The scribes teach that Elijah must come before the Messiah.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Elijah does indeed come, and he will restore all things.
passages.sermon: Jesus answered them.\r\nJesus said, “Elijah does come.\r\nElijah will restore all things.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα

passages.text: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but have done to him whatever they wished. In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Elijah has already come.”
The people did not recognize Elijah.
They did whatever they wanted to him.
In the same way, the Son of Man will suffer at their hands.
The Son of Man refers to Jesus.
The people will cause Jesus to suffer.
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν οὕτως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: Then the disciples understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He referred to someone.
The disciples listened to Jesus.
They realized Jesus was talking about John the Baptist.
passages.original: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: When they came to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt before Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus and His disciples came to a crowd.\r\nA man approached Jesus.\r\nThe man knelt before Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν

passages.text: “Lord, have mercy on my son,” he said. “He has seizures and is suffering terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
passages.sermon:
A man came to Jesus and knelt before Him.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Lord, have mercy on my son.”
He explained his son’s condition.
He said, “My son has seizures.”
He said, “He suffers greatly.”
He said, “He often falls into the fire.”
He said, “He often falls into the water.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγων Κύριε ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ

passages.text: I brought him to Your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
passages.sermon: A man brought his son to Jesus’ disciples.\r\nThe disciples tried to heal the boy.\r\nThe disciples could not heal him.
passages.original: καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι

passages.text: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called them an unbelieving generation.
He called them a perverse generation.
He asked, “How long must I stay with you?”
He asked, “How long must I put up with you?”
He said, “Bring the boy here to Me.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη ἕως πότε μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἔσομαι ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε

passages.text: Then Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, and he was healed from that moment.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the boy.
The boy had a demon.
Jesus spoke sharply to the demon.
The demon left the boy.
The boy became well at that moment.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης

passages.text: Afterward the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
They came to Him in private.
They spoke to Jesus alone.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
passages.original: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπον Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό

passages.text: “Because you have so little faith,” He answered. “For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He answered their question.
He said, “You have little faith.
I tell you the truth.
If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can speak to this mountain.
You can say, ‘Move from here to there.’
The mountain will move.
Nothing will be impossible for you.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ καὶ μεταβήσεται καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν

passages.text: When they gathered together in Galilee, Jesus told them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.
passages.sermon: Jesus gathered with His disciples in Galilee.\r\nJesus spoke to them.\r\nJesus said, “The Son of Man will soon be handed over to men.”
passages.original: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μέλλει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: They will kill Him, and on the third day He will be raised to life.” And the disciples were deeply grieved.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said that men will kill Him.
He said that on the third day He will rise to life.
The disciples heard this.
The disciples became very sad.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα

passages.text: After they had arrived in Capernaum, the collectors of the two-drachma tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your Teacher pay the two drachmas?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples arrived in Capernaum.
The collectors of the two-drachma tax approached Peter.
They spoke to Peter.
They asked Peter a question.
They said, “Does your Teacher pay the two-drachma tax?”
passages.original: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα

passages.text: “Yes,” he answered. When Peter entered the house, Jesus preempted him. “What do you think, Simon?” He asked. “From whom do the kings of the earth collect customs and taxes: from their own sons, or from others?”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter answered, “Yes.”
Peter then entered the house.
Jesus spoke to Peter first.
Jesus said, “What do you think, Simon?”
Jesus asked, “The kings of the earth collect customs and taxes.”
Jesus asked, “Do they collect from their own sons?”
Jesus asked, “Or do they collect from others?”
passages.original: Λέγει Ναί Καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Τί σοι δοκεῖ Σίμων οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων

passages.text: “From others,” Peter answered. “Then the sons are exempt,” Jesus declared.
passages.sermon: Peter answered, “From others.”\r\nJesus spoke to Peter.\r\nJesus said, “Then the sons are free.”
passages.original: Εἰπόντος δέ Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἄρα¦Γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί

passages.text: “But so that we may not offend them, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a four-drachma coin. Take it and give it to them for My tax and yours.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus wanted to avoid offending the tax collectors.
Jesus gave Peter instructions.
Jesus said, “Go to the sea.”
“Cast a hook into the water.”
“Catch the first fish that comes up.”
“Open the mouth of that fish.”
“You will find a four-drachma coin inside.”
“Take the coin.”
“Give it to the collectors.”
“This will pay the tax for Me and for you.”
passages.original: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ
